label: rem:markov-trace-ambient-s3
title: The ambient three-sphere $S^3$ is the target of the Alexander--Markov correspondence: $\mathrm{tr}_M$ is by construction a link invariant in $S^3$
html:
Remark. The ambient three-sphere S^3 is the target of the Alexander--Markov correspondence: \mathrm{tr}_M is by construction a link invariant in S^3

The ambient three-sphere S^3 enters strictly through the closure construction via two classical theorems.

Alexander's theorem states that every oriented link in S^3 is the closure of some braid. Therefore, the disjoint union of braid groups exhausts all link types in the three-sphere.

Markov's theorem establishes that two braids have isotopic closures in S^3 if and only if they are related by a sequence of conjugation and stabilisation moves.

The Markov trace is invariant under both moves. Because closure surjects onto the links of S^3 and its fibres are exactly the Markov-move orbits, the Markov trace descends to a well-defined invariant of links in S^3. The ambient S^3 is thus constructed categorically as the target of the Alexander--Markov correspondence, rather than posited geometrically upstream.

The closure construction fixes this ambient S^3 independently of the gauge group, which enters only through the representation category. Whether the coincidence \mathrm{SU}(2) \cong S^3 is structural or incidental here remains open: the Reeb bundle presents a three-sphere as the total space of the Hopf fibration S^3 \to \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2, which is the coset projection \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathrm{SU}(2)/U(1), and under that reading the two are the same object. We do not settle the identification here.
